security_audit.summary: Of 55 alerts, 54 are false positives involving Markdown, readable Chinese text, service links, identifiers, or scoped credential checks. One confirmed risk involves automatically executing an unpinned npm package with access to the agent environment. No evidence found of embedded credentials, credential exfiltration, reconnaissance, encoded payloads, or prompt injection in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The direct CLI examples use npx -y socialdatax-skills@latest, executing a mutable package without an installation confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed CLI version, verify package provenance, and require approval before first execution in an environment with credentials.

content.user_title: Analyze WeChat Channels Video Structure and Feedback
content.value_statement: Popular videos can be difficult to explain from engagement counts alone. This skill combines available details, transcripts, and sampled comments into an evidence-based creative analysis.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve available public video details from a WeChat Channels link or share text through SocialDataX CLI or configured MCP tools.
Submit speech transcription tasks and query an existing job without resubmitting the video.
Analyze opening hooks, content structure, spoken pacing, and interaction prompts using returned descriptions and transcripts.
Retrieve sampled comments and selected reply threads, reporting pagination scope and incomplete results.
Suggest three to five reusable creative approaches while separating public facts, transcript evidence, comment evidence, and interpretation.
Export SRT subtitles through CLI version 0.2.64 or newer when requested and valid timed segments are available.
limitations: Requires authenticated SocialDataX access and sufficient service credits; direct CLI also requires Node.js, npm, and network access.
Conclusions cover only the supplied video and returned samples, not complete platform coverage, hidden demographics, or recommendation mechanisms.
Missing transcripts, metrics, or timestamps limit analysis; hosted MCP alone does not create a local SRT file.
Does not publish, log in, modify accounts, or guarantee viral results; reviewed files do not include the external CLI implementation.

use_cases.title: Develop a video outline
use_cases.description: Analyze a reference video's hook and structure, then identify transferable approaches supported by the returned transcript.

use_cases.title: Research audience questions
use_cases.description: Review a bounded comment sample and selected replies to identify recurring questions, objections, and possible follow-up topics.

use_cases.title: Prepare an editorial case study
use_cases.description: Separate public metrics, transcript evidence, audience comments, and interpretation in a structured report with explicit sampling limits.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze one video
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this WeChat Channels video: [link or share text]. Use available details and its transcript. Identify the opening hook, structure, and missing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review audience feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [video link] using details, transcript, and one comment page. Summarize repeated questions and objections. Do not retrieve replies. State the sample limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: add a bounded audience feedback sample.

prompt_templates.title: Develop reusable approaches
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [video link] for [target audience]. Separate facts from interpretations. Propose three to five reusable approaches with supporting evidence. Mark missing data and avoid performance guarantees.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: convert evidence into creative directions.

prompt_templates.title: Resume transcription and export subtitles
prompt_templates.prompt: Query existing transcription job [job_id] without resubmitting. If successful, analyze its hook and structure. Export SRT to [new writable path] only if valid timed segments exist.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: resume a task and request a local subtitle file.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: analyze a supplied video whose opening transcript asks, 'Why does your first sentence lose viewers?' No comments are returned.
output: Opening hook: the question names a specific viewer problem and creates an information gap.
Structure and spoken pacing: cannot assess the full sequence from the opening excerpt alone.
Comment feedback: unavailable because no comment sample was returned.
Reusable angle: begin with a concrete audience question, then support the answer with evidence.
Limits: the excerpt does not establish why the video performed well.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: resume an existing transcription job and export subtitles, but the completed response has no valid timed segments.
output: Task status: the existing transcription job completed.
Subtitle export: no local SRT file was generated because valid timed segments were unavailable.
Recovery: retain the returned transcript and explain the export limitation without inventing timestamps or resubmitting the video.

best_practices: Provide the complete video link, share text, or existing job identifier, and define comment and reply limits before retrieval.
Keep credentials in supported secret storage, approve CLI execution, and use a reviewed package version rather than a mutable latest release.
Keep facts, transcript evidence, comment samples, and interpretations separate; reuse job identifiers and continuation tokens when recovering partial results.
anti_patterns: Treating sampled comments or public engagement counts as proof of platform ranking rules or guaranteed future performance.
Pasting API keys into chat, logs, screenshots, or tracked files, or concatenating raw user input into shell commands.
Resubmitting existing transcription jobs, repeatedly retrying insufficient-balance errors, or restarting partial pagination from the first page.

faq.question: What input can I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a WeChat Channels video link, share text, or an existing transcription job identifier.

faq.question: Do I need an API key and Node.js?
faq.answer: Direct CLI requires a SocialDataX API key and Node.js/npm. An authenticated hosted MCP connection does not require local CLI credentials or Node.js.

faq.question: What happens when the transcript is unavailable?
faq.answer: The report marks transcript-dependent conclusions as unavailable. It does not invent dialogue, timestamps, or unseen video structure.

faq.question: Can it export subtitles?
faq.answer: Yes, through CLI 0.2.64 or newer when valid timed segments exist. The destination must be new and its parent directory writable.

faq.question: Can it publish content or guarantee viral results?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes returned public data without account actions and does not guarantee reach, engagement, or recommendation outcomes.

faq.question: What should I do if a task fails or credits run out?
faq.answer: Keep any job identifier and partial results. Resolve authentication or balance issues, then resume the same job or pagination position without duplicate submissions.
